title: Telemetry for Monitoring Temperature and Activity in Mice
author: John Rutledge
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ywtfxen

steps.title: Prepare Mice for Surgery
steps.instruction: Anesthetize mice and prepare the surgical site.

substeps.instruction: Shave and disinfect the flank and back.

steps.title: Implant Transmitter Subcutaneously (Flank Option)
steps.instruction: Implant the transmitter body in a subcutaneous pouch along the right flank.

substeps.instruction: Create a subcutaneous pouch along the right flank via a ventral neck incision.

Use blunt dissecting scissors (Fine Science Tools, catalog no. 14018-14) to gently dissect skin from underlying tissue, starting at the right neck region and proceeding posteriorly to form a pocket large enough to house the transmitter without stretching the skin.
Lubricate the pocket by inserting the tip of a 1mL syringe containing warmed saline.
Slip the transmitter under the skin into the pocket, positioning it as close to the right hindlimb as possible.
Apply a small drop of veterinary adhesive to the catheter in the right neck region to secure the device.
Close the neck incision using 1 or 2 wound clips and seal with tissue adhesive.

steps.title: Implant Transmitter on Back (Alternative Option)
steps.instruction: Install the transmitter body at the midscapular region of the back.

substeps.instruction: Shave the upper back and make a horizontal incision.
Place the transmitter in the opening and suture it to both the muscle and the skin (with the suture loop around the probe) via the suture rib on the probe.
Make a separate ventral neck incision and tunnel the catheter subcutaneously to the neck to carry out the catheterization procedure.

steps.title: Post-Surgical Recovery and Analgesia
steps.instruction: Provide post-operative care and pain management.

substeps.instruction: Keep mice warm on a heating pad and monitor closely until fully recovered from anesthesia.
Administer Buprenex (buprenorphine hydrochloride) 0.1 mg/kg subcutaneously at the termination of surgery.

steps.title: Return to Home Cages and Activation
steps.instruction: Return recovered mice to home cages and activate monitoring.

substeps.instruction: Place mice in home cages situated atop telemetry receivers.
Magnetically activate radiotelemeters immediately upon return to the home cage.
Monitor mice daily for general condition, body weight, food and water intake, surgical wound healing, and signs of morbidity.

steps.title: Collect Radiotelemetry Data
steps.instruction: Continuously record and store physiological data using the Dataquest ART data acquisition system (Data Sciences International).

substeps.instruction: Record temperature and locomotor activity continuously.
Sample data every 5 min for 10-s intervals.
Plot MAP and HR data collected from the first 12 consecutive days following surgery as mean values over each hour.
